utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. The affirmation still applies. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You remember on Friday towards the end we discussed and reviewed your report on the events in Ljuboten 10th to 12th August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 511 of your report and until paragraph 538 you deal with the events at Ljuboten on the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown his report, 5466 -- P466, page 146 in the English and 156 in the Macedonian version, paragraph 522.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You see it in front of you, Witness?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on the top of the page so that we see the paragraph 522, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In paragraph 522, you say in the sentence begins in the third row, the document states that the terrorists attacked Macedonian security forces in the area of Ljubanci at 1540." Namely, more than seven hours after Johan Tarculovski police unit entered Ljuboten. Could you tell me where did this information come from, that it was a police unit of Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are numerous reports, specifically the reports of the army of the Republic of Macedonia, which suggest that the units of men in police uniforms under command of Mr. Tarculovski entered Ljuboten. One of those reports is the report by Colonel Kopacev, I think, and the other report like this is the report of Captain Kostadinov.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: However, is it correct that there is no document where it reads that it was Johan Tarculovski's police unit and that they were under the command of Johan Tarculovski, that is your conclusion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that a number of documents, mostly the Macedonian army documents but also some documents of the Ministry of Interior, indicate that this unit was indeed under command of Mr. Tarculovski, and this unit arrived to the area of Ljuboten, at least in the evening of the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in your report, you mention the 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the date where the unit actually entered Ljuboten and when the fighting in the village and around the village occurred. But I think the unit arrived in the area of Ljuboten and in fact overnighted in Ljubanci, specifically in the rest house where a unit of the Macedonian army was also located during the night between 10 and 11 August.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But is it correct that the only document where it is mentioned literally, and I quote, "Johan Tarculovski police unit" is the indictment itself and your report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I'm afraid I will have to refer you to specific documents. If you just give me one minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Just tell me which is the document and I will ask the registry to display it.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Fine. Let's start with document P00303.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown the Exhibit P00303.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Can you scroll down the page little bit? Can you go to the next page, please. Actually, let's start from this page first. And let's read the very first sentence. "On 10 August 2001 at 2130 hours a group of around 40 persons came to the school in the village of Ljubanci. The group was headed by the person Johan Tarculovski, head of the agency Kometa."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could I stop you here.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you sure that Johan Tarculovski is the head of the Kometa agency?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure about that, and I don't think I mentioned this in my report. But in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where does it read here that it was a police unit of Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says in the same paragraph in the middle it: "The persons were wearing MVR uniforms." MVR stands for Ministry of Internal Affairs, as you are probably aware, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where does it read in this section that it was a police unit of Johan Tarculovski? Can you read that sentence?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I understand my analytical experience is sufficient enough to link up certain things and make references to certain accents and facts which are mentioned in one document. I don't really think that you really have to refer to any direct sweeping statements like this. It is pretty clear from this paragraph that, A, at this specific time, a group of around 30 persons came to the school in Ljubanci; B, this group was under command of Mr. Johan Tarculovski; C, these persons were wearing MVR uniforms. How would you interpret these three facts yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you tell me where did you see that it was a group under the command of Johan Tarculovski? Could you quote this part of the report?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second line on this document clearly says the group was headed by person Johan Tarculovski. If you go throughout this document in its entirety you will see that it also contains a number of references to Mr. Tarculovski. And these references, if analysed clearly, would suggest that in fact he was the person who was in command of this group, as is clear from the subsequent actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you agree with me that in this document it is not mentioned, I quote, that the group was under the command of Johan Tarculovski, and in this document it is not mentioned that it was a police unit of Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid the difference here, or, rather, the implication that are you make something purely semantic. In fact, if you read the second sentence again in Macedonian language it says: "The group was led by Johan Tarculovski." I think perhaps if we really analyse the sentence in Macedonian, it is even more clear to suggest that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was leading this group. In other words, he was in command of this group. Before we actually continue, could I kindly ask the usher to adjust my chair, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Sorry, I don't know how to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, I understand Macedonian language, so I would like to follow up on this. Being led in Macedonia can mean that one was at the front of the group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, that could also mean this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So having led it does not necessarily mean that he was a commander of the group.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My interpretation would be different. I think I have expressed my view sufficiently enough, but if you would like to get some more indications, we can just go through this document again. In fact, in the same paragraph the following is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in this paragraph there is no word in the sense of command?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can the witness please be permitted to finish his last answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There's no problem about that. I'm sure Mr. Apostolski was unaware the witness was continuing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You will probably note that in the same paragraph the following is stated: "These persons asked Major Mitre Despodov who is commander of the 3rd Guardist Battalion to provide them with a place to sleep in the mountain lodge in the village of Ljubanci. Major Despodov asked them on whose orders they had come. They said that this is known to the president and no one else should know about their stay. Major Despodov asked them what their role is there, they answered that they have the task to enter the village of Ljuboten and to conduct a search and cleaning of the terrain." As you can see, this paragraph doesn't really mention any other person except Mr. Johan Tarculovski who might hypothetically be in the command of this unit. But can you go to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can I just ask you here before we go on to the next page. Is it correct that this paragraph you read does not mention that Johan Tarculovski was the commander of his police unit, as you call it?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I mentioned, sir, my interpretation of this paragraph is different. This is a military document and was written by a military person. The more so, this person was in fact the officer for security and counter-intelligence. I think when he was writing this document he meant very well and he understood the precise science of command in the military way, suggesting that "led" in Macedonian version of this document would literally mean under command or commanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But that is your conjecture. When I asked you about the Macedonian language you answered that it was possible that he was at the front of the group, that this could be the meaning of the word "led."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would rather say it is not my conjecture but, rather, my analysis. But we are just discussing one page of this document only. There are other pages as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: We could open the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the second page opened, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Maybe you could refer to the Sunday, 12th of August, because in your report you speak about the 12th of August when the police units of Johan Tarculovski was led by him. If you could read the report that refers only about Sunday, so that we can save time?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather continue day by day, Mr. Apostolski, just for the sake of completeness of the analysis. I think in an exercise like this it is not really advisable to drop anything which might actually otherwise be of importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I draw your attention to the second paragraph of the document in Macedonian, and the third paragraph of the same document in English. The third paragraph in English says again: On Saturday, 11 August 2001, the above-listed persons headed by Johan Tarculovski conducted reconnaissance in the village of Ljuboten and in the village they shot at dogs that barked at them. Around 1700 hours to 1730 hours, the person Johan Tarculovski asked Major Mitre Despodov to shoot at targets in the village Ljuboten, which they previously had determined precisely together with major Mitre Despodov. Major Despodov did not want to open fire upon the above-mentioned targets without orders, requested approval from his superiors." I think this is sufficiently clear from the paragraph which I have just quoted though I have not really quoted it in full that, again, A --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you just tell me -- okay, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you sir. So it is sufficiently clear, I think, that, A, this group of persons was headed by Mr. Tarculovski; B, his intention was to conduct reconnaissance of the village of Ljuboten; and C, there was some kind of arrangement or agreement to open fire at the targets in the village of Ljuboten. From the military point of view a reconnaissance presents an important step towards carrying out a certain operation or an action. I don't really think that such a reconnaissance could actually have been conducted without a certain prearranged plan, which serves as an indication that a certain action was supposed to take in the village of Ljuboten in the next few hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that it is nowhere mentioned that it is a police unit commanded by Johan Tarculovski. Here it is mentioned above-mentioned persons led by Johan Tarculovski. "Led" in Macedonian language means to be in front of everybody, not that somebody is the leader of the group.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this word has probably more than one meaning, sir, and it is very easy in fact to establish just by looking up an appropriate dictionary. But if we come again to the issue of who specifically was in charge of this group, we can go to the next paragraph, which again says: "On Sunday, 12 of August 2001, at 0430 hours, 0430 hours the person Johan Tarculovski with the other persons (MVR reservists)," and we know that MVR stands for Ministry of Interior, "started the action." I don't know if this is a sufficient comment on my part, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Could you please tell me where you see that it is stated that the person Johan Tarculovski was leading or was commanding?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Would you please show me the place where?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this particular paragraph which I just quoted it says, "the person Johan Tarculovski with the other persons." Well, I think in this paragraph the special role of Mr. Tarculovski is clearly visible by the mere fact that he is mentioned by person and no one else is.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But this is your conclusion. We cannot see that in the document.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my analysis; this is not my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. It is your analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness be shown 65 ter 2D404, page 2D05-0052, paragraph 68. That is the indictment against Mr. Ljube Boskoski and Mr. Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The paragraph 68 says: "On Sunday, 11th of August 2001, the presence of armed Albanian combatants was estimated to maximum 10 to 15 persons armed with automatic weaponry or at least one machine-gun. These individuals were acting either alone or in some groups to oppose to the advancing of the police units of Johan Tarculovski." Is this the only place where you could read that this was a police unit of Johan Tarculovski?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. I think the document which we have just discussed sufficiently suggest that these men were dressed in police uniforms, which is, for me, a sufficient basis to draw an assessment that they in fact were the reserve policemen. In fact, this is what this document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But did you check the facts that are written in this document we just considered? For example, that Johan Tarculovski was the owner of the agency Kometa. So as a start, I would ask that you question.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a number of documents originating from the Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Macedonia which seemed to clearly suggest that there was an investigation at some point of time made in the ministry at which Mr. Tarculovski was asked to answer a number of questions related to the events in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you see a document, not a statement?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen a document and I don't think it was a statement. I think it was a document which was signed by Mr. Ramicevic, the liaison officer of the Ministry of Interior of Republic of Macedonia to the International Tribunal for Former Yugoslavia. This document clearly says that Mr. Johan Tarculovski was in Ljuboten with a group of men whom he selected personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And that is your conclusion in your report.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, which conclusion you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From -- what you read from Mr. Besim Ramicevic, what you read in the document.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no reasons to question the authenticity of the document nor the facts mentioned in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Once again, I would like to ask you whether your report and the indictment are the only two documents that I'm now quoting you where it is mentioned a police unit commanded by Johan Tarculovski.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. Another document which seems to suggest exactly the same information is document P00304.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But not even in this document in any place it is said that we're talking about the police unit commanded by Johan Tarculovski. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you may wish to take a look at this document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I have seen this document, and I have not found anywhere in this document that it is a police unit commanded by Johan Tarculovski. Have you come across this? That's my question. And, once again, I would like to quote, "police unit under the command of Johan Tarculovski."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Speaking specifically of the document P00304, this document is signed by Colonel Kapacov, the commander of the 1st Guardist Brigade. This document seems to be based on numerous interviews of the military officers of the Macedonian army, who were present in the area of Ljuboten in the period between 10 and 12 August 2001. This document is consistent with the document P00303, which we have just discussed. And specifically answering your question, it, again, speaks of a unit of men led by Mr. Johan Tarculovski and dressed in police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you suggest that this document states, I'm quoting, "police unit under the command of Johan Tarculovski."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying that these two documents, at least these two documents, not to mention the document I mentioned previously originating -- the one originating from the Ministry of Interior, gives perhaps sufficient grounds for any analyst to note certain consistencies as well as to draw certain indications that seem to suggest that the group of men which entered Ljuboten were indeed police reservists dressed in police uniforms. I really doubt if anywhere else in the territory of Macedonia or for that matter throughout the conflict there could develop a situation where an unknown group of men dressed in police uniforms could take part in any armed action. This could happen only in case this was a unit which was somehow associated with the official bodies of state power. In this sense, the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But this is also your conclusion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My analysis, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now I would like to go to another topic about the chronology of events which is an integral part of your report. Mr. Bezruchenko, whether an attack on a passenger plane as a terrorist attack.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I think we've had a sufficient discussion regarding the issue of terrorism, and perhaps I would be repeating myself and I would say again that the main distinction between terrorism and the war is that terrorism essentially negates combat. Terrorism tends to attack targets which cannot respond in kind; that is, they have no arms. In other words, these are armed attacks against unarmed targets. So if you're asking me whether an attack on a passenger plane is a terrorist act or not, well, I would like to ask you a question first. Which attack you are referring to and whether it is mentioned in my report?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you as a military expert to respond to my question whether an attack on a passenger plane is a terrorist attack or not, in general.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general that would be regarded as a terrorist attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Whether -- could you tell me whether an attack on a passenger train is a terrorist attack?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This would -- this could be the case, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is a kidnapping of a journalist a terrorist attack or a terrorist action?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's very difficult to say. I would imagine it would depend on the specific situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your opinion, Mr. Bezruchenko, the military conflict in Macedonia in 2001 in January, you divide this conflict into two stages. The first stage starts at January with an attack of NLA on the police station in Tearce and ends on the 25th of March with the taking of the Kale in Tetovo by the Macedonian security forces. The second stage begins in May with the opening of the Kumanovo-Lipkovo front and ends with the conclusion of the Ohrid Agreement and the disarmament of the members of NLA. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You identify the month of April as a relatively peaceful period.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say it was peaceful as such, because the armed attacks in April continued. I think I indicated only that it was a period of relative lull in the combat activities and general scope of the activities was somewhat limited as compared to such months of heavy activities as March, May, June, July, August, and February.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm quoting your conclusion about the chronology of the armed conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is my assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And here you say that -- that in April there was a relatively calm period. So you identify this period as pretty calm. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I just mentioned, sir, and perhaps I would have to repeat it again just to make certain that there is no misunderstanding. The month of April indeed saw a somewhat subsided activity as compared to the other months when the war was going on in Macedonia. We should not really forget the fact that one of the most bloody ambushes during the entire conflict took place in April in which, if I recall correctly, about a dozen of Macedonian soldiers and policemen were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you finish your answer?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: But just to give you a detailed answer, in fact, I would probably refer you to paragraphs 42 through 48 of my report, which speaks about the activities in April 2001. This ambush actually took place on the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like us to review the chronology of events. And if the witness can be shown his report, 566 [as interpreted], page 104. Could you please read aloud what you wrote about that month, about the armed conflict, what was your conclusion.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on this page in --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Where it starts with: "The armed conflict."

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. "The armed conflict in Macedonia can be subdivided into two phases. The first phase began in January 2001 with a NLA attack on the police station in Tearce and ended in March with governments forces occupation of Kale hill on the Tetovo front. There was a period of relative lull in April. The second phase began in early May, with the opening of the Kumanovo-Lipkovo front. The second phase ended with the Ohrid Agreement and NLA disarmament and demobilisation."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I said this because I mentioned previously about the month of April. You concluded that the month was a relatively calm period. Let us stick to January now. According to the chronology of the armed conflict in January, you say that there was an armed conflict and then you state, point 2: "As actions that held -- that happened on January 22, one policeman was killed," and according to you it was a military action. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And under point 3, you say: "On January 26, there was a fire on a passenger train that was travelling from Skopje to Kicevo in the area of Zajas and Stragonmiste, north of Kicevo. The projectile of unidentified calibre penetrated the windows of the train and nobody was injured." Is this according to your opinion a military operation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apparently in this particular case this attack was not aimed at a military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in the chronology you state this as a military operation as a part of the chronology of the military armed conflict in Macedonia. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is indeed the chronology of the armed conflict in Macedonia. Since it addresses the events of military nature, various actions combats, operations, attacks, manoeuvres, deployments and so on. But compiling this chronology of course I could not really avoid certain acts of attendant violence, including the plight of the civilians and the issue of the refugees and displaced persons. In fact, in this consideration I was guided by similar chronologies which have been compiled by various international agencies covering the wars in Croatia and Bosnia. This is exactly the same analogy here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in this case it was a terrorist attack on a train?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could be. If this was a civilian train, this could be a terrorist attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In your report, it is stated that it was a passenger train. So now could you agree with me that regarding the month of January, you have specified two events: One is a military attack in your opinion, and that is the attack on the terrorist on --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: -- on the police station in Tearce and the second event is the attack on the passenger train on the 26th of January, and you stated now that it has been a terrorist act, considering that in January it was only those two events that you had identified, how did you ascertain that the NLA was a military force in January and it was not a terrorist organisation?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Answering your question, I would like to point out the following. First of all, the military activities in January were not limited to attacks by the NLA only, but also included the activities by the Macedonian security forces. As you see, on January 30th, the spokesperson of the Ministry of Defence, Mr. Trendafilov, stated that armed forces had been increased at check-points and watch towers along the border with Serbia and Kosovo. A number of other documents also suggest that there was a considerable build-up of forces of the NLA on the border between Kosovo and Macedonia. This is an important military activity which suggests a period of preparation for major activities. Of course, in my analysis I could not overlook these activities, though this is not something which would -- could be regarded as a direct military attack. Secondly, as you rightly mentioned, in paragraph 2 I speak about the NLA attack at the police station in the village of Tearce. This was the first serious attack by the NLA at what can be described as a legitimate target, since this was a police station. This means -- or, rather, this leads me to believe that the armed conflict that is in terms of direct military confrontation began in January 2001. For this reason, it doesn't really matter how many other attacks actually occurred during this month.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But wouldn't your assertion be partial in January, considering that there was one terrorist and one military action, as you say yourself, to say that in January the uprising of the NLA took place in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't quite see what you mean, sir. For the reasons which I have just explained, it is pretty clear that the beginning of the conflict can actually be traced to January. There were numerous indications that this conflict was about to break out. These indications were provided by the Macedonian intelligence and security services, clearly indicating that there were numerous groups crossing the border from Kosovo into Macedonia. These groups were armed, these groups were trained and they were equipped for not picking mushrooms, if I can say so, but for actual fighting. This was pretty serious situation and this indeed indicated the beginning on the conflict. Coming back to the issue of terrorism which you have just raised again, I would like to reiterate that throughout my report the methodology which I was guided by was to separate the issue of terrorism from the issue of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I will ask you to provide brief answers in the interest of time, if that is possible for to you do it. So could we please now look at the second page of the document. This is your chronological overview of the month of February.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You say here regarding the month of February that the military conflict was transferred to the northern part of the country to the border with Tanusevci, border with Kosovo, SFRY and the increased presence of forces was noted towards middle of February and severe battles with -- between the Macedonian force and the [indiscernible] started towards the end of the month -- towards the middle of the month. In paragraph 5 you say on February 16 an armed group belonging to the NLA kidnapped a team of journalists from the A1 television and then you say that the NLA searched journalists and their vehicles and seized their equipment and then set them free. In your opinion, was there a military operation of the NLA on the 16th of February and please provide a brief answer, if you can.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the fact that the NLA actually captured the village of Tanusevci was a military operation. I think I have already explained previously that Tanusevci was regarded as a particularly important location on the border because it served, apparently, for many years as a major transit point for smuggling weapons and ammunition and --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, could you please answer my question directly. Was the kidnapping of journalists of a TV station whereby their vehicles and equipment were confiscated a military operation, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I'm saying, sir. This particular operation, that is, taking the journalists hostage as well as taking away their equipment, was certainly not a military operation. More so, the Macedonian public actually learned about the presence of the NLA in the Macedonian territory precisely because of this very incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So before that, the NLA existed but nobody was aware that it existed because the public learned about this from the journalists?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was the overriding perception, well, at least in the broad Macedonian public.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Further on you state, in paragraph 8 that armed clashes between the NLA and Macedonian security forces occurred on February 26, 27 and 28 in and around Tanusevci. In your opinion, were these two actions, one kidnapping of a team of journalists and the other, armed clashes towards the end of the month in Tanusevci, is this a sufficient proof of the existence of an uprising in the Republic of Macedonia by the NLA? And the existence of an armed conflict in Macedonia in February 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I will agree with you, in a sense, that February saw the further escalation of the conflict which actually began in January. You mentioned -- or, rather, you asked if the kidnapping of a team of journalists and armed conflicts or armed clashes towards the end of the month were sufficient proof of the existence of an uprising. Well, my answer would be that in February there were sufficient indications to suggest that there was a very serious danger of full-scale uprising as well as the escalation of violence. Well, whether the fact of taking the journalists is actually linked in any way to the armed fighting in the village of Tanusevci is very difficult to say. They simply probably found themselves there at the wrong time and in the wrong place.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Tanusevci, in February, 26, 27 and the 28th, no member of the Macedonian security force was killed??

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not certain if anyone was killed on these three specific days in Tanusevci. I think there were some casualties among the NLA, though. And I think the first casualties that the Macedonian security forces actually suffered were as early as January while the attack on Tearce.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But in February no member of the Macedonian security forces was killed.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see from my chronology, apparently not.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So your assertion that in February there were heavy battles between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces would not be correct, considering the fact that there were no killed members of the Macedonian security forces.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, a list of the combat casualties of the Macedonian army and police is provided by the "White Book", which was released by the Macedonian Ministry of Interior. But I don't think that it provides the full list, since, as I mentioned previously, the actual number of casualties, as is clear from the report of the Ministry of Interior, is almost 150 men higher than the official number. 150 men higher as the official number provided by the "White Book". So I would assume in fact that perhaps were there some casualties suffered by the Macedonian security forces but they were simply not made public.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And does it also hold true regarding the action in Ljuboten, in August 2001, because you say that you haven't seen in any document that a member of Macedonian security forces was killed or injured?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course that could be a possibility as well and this is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Seen any document suggesting that someone was killed in Macedonia -- I mean in Ljuboten, among the security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And could we look at the following page, dealing the month of March. You say in your conclusion -- your conclusion regarding March, "At the beginning of March the armed conflict continued and significantly escalated in the area around the village of Tanusevci and the region of Skopska Crna Gora with increased number of clashes between the NLA and the Macedonian security forces. The KFOR increased the attempts to patrol the Kosovo side of the border and detained several suspected members of the NLA. Could you tell me why would KFOR detain NLA members, if that was a legal, legitimate armed group and fighters for human rights, if they were that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Apostolski, I think I never said in my report, and for that matter elsewhere, throughout my testimony, that I considered the NLA a legal armed group. If I did so, please let me know which particular portion of the report I mentioned this.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But why would the KFOR arrest them, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: The government of Macedonia was cooperating with the NATO forces in its territory which were in fact were a part of KFOR contingent and there were a number of agreements made between the government and NATO to the effect to insulate the border from various groups which were trying to cross it from Kosovo into Macedonia and from Macedonia into Kosovo. This was important activity aimed at curbing the armed violence in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the KFOR was not supporting the activities of the NLA in any way?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think we can say that KFOR was supporting the activities on the NLA. That would be entirely wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now about some different issues. As a military expert, particularly since you come from the former Soviet Union and the Warsaw Pact, you are aware of the rocket launcher Strela, arrow 2?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I know this system.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And within the Warsaw Pact, Strela, arrow, 2M were used?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is in fact a portable [Realtime transcript read in error "potable"] shoulder-launched missile with an infrared seeker which is homing on the nozzle of a flying aircraft. This model is pretty common in many countries of the world, including former Yugoslavia, despite the fact that Yugoslavia was never a member of the Warsaw Pact. It is true that this missile was actually used in the conflict in Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the rocket arrow 2M was moving towards the reflection from the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat his quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: It is not in the transcript. Could you please confirm this?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask the counsel to repeat his question because the interpreters could not follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Better results are attained in the fight against helicopters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before we actually proceed further, I would like to correct the script, specifically line 24/1. I think this particular paragraph should read as follows: There is in fact a portable, p-o-r-t-a-b-l-e, not potable, portable shoulder-launched missile with infrared seeker, s-e-e-k-e-r, which is homing on the nozzle of flying aircraft. Now coming back to your question, whether better results are obtained in the fight against helicopters. Well, I wouldn't really say so. Actually this depends on a specific situation and how this missile is used. It depends on the flight of the -- direction of the flight of the aircraft, the weather, whether it is day-time or night-time, the position of the sun, and some other things. But generally speaking it is of course easier to shoot down a slow flying helicopter than a fast jet.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And a parallel to Strela 2 is the light portable rocket launcher system, Stinger: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. This is in fact --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In page 6502 of the transcript, 5 and 6, you say that there were similar in their design, if you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily in design by in principle operation. I think both of them are based on the principle of homing on the source of heat radiation of a flying aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would say it was the reflection of the aircraft. Could you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which reflection do you mean? If you mean the radar reflection, this is something else. For this purpose there would be an entirely different principle applied, the principle of radar guidance. This is the self-guided home seeker equipped missile.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No, no. Both rockets, Strela 2 and the Stinger, have the same fire-power. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Essentially they belong to the same class. This is the class of portable shoulder-launched anti-aircraft missiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that they have the same firing power?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you actually mean by "firing power"? Do you mean --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From a military aspect, the same firing power, do they have that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the range, they probably would have about the same range. If you mean the payload, that is the weight of the warhead, well, I'm not sure about these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do they have the same payload of explosive or similar?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think approximately the same. Perhaps Stinger would have a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps this is the convenient time for the break? And I will then have -- I apologise, there is still time. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you remember that you testified about the trainings inside the NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall that you suggested that such training was the essential part of the efficient functioning of the army formation, the page 6503 of the transcript?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir, which army you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Generally speaking, any army formation and specifically about the NLA.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recall that you saw a document where the number of the alleged training camps of the NLA was mentioned. For the transcript exhibit P485, page 13.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be difficult for me, sir, at this point to recall which specific document you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the witness could be shown P485, page 13. Page 13 in English version. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Have you seen a documented evidence about any of these alleged camps for training?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean probably if I have seen any other document which would suggest corroboration of the existence of these training camps?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No. Have you seen any documented evidence about any of these camps --

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: -- that would confirm the existence of these training camps in Pescopeja in Albania, for example?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in fact, apart from this document, I have seen other documents originating from the directorate for security and counter-intelligence of the Macedonian Ministry of Interior, which appears to be broadly consistent with this document in addressing this issue. It also mentions a number of localities both in Macedonia and out of Macedonia which were apparently used by the NLA as training facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But have you seen any evidence that comes from these camps? Just reply with yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Evidence coming from these camps?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you seen any record of trainees that attended these camps or this kind of training?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think I have seen any list of personnel which has taken any training in these camps.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen any evidence about instructors that should -- that were leading this training?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember some documents coming from the Ministry of Interior as well as from the Ministry of Defence suggesting some names of instructors who were running training in some of those camps. But I don't think I remember those names.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen any manuals about this kind of training?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the fact that somebody would assert that this training happened was enough for you to believe that it was the case?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was not just somebody who was asserting that. In this specific case, I was dealing with one of the most fundamental documents on the NLA and one of the most important ones which had been prepared by the intelligence sector of the Ministry of Defence, and I had no reasons to doubt this document, because I believe the Macedonian Ministry of Defence sector of intelligence employs sufficiently qualified personnel in these matters to make these kinds of analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: The documents that come, as you say, from Albanian sources, you have not seen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did I understand correctly your testimony, that -- that NLA has established a disciplinary system on its level. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really think that I said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question. Last week you said that there was a lot of crimes committed during the crisis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So I assume this would imply crimes committed by NLA. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as I mentioned previously, the criminality was not really specifically the subject of my report. In any war, criminality is a significant and attendant factor, suffice it to mention the history of the Second World War, for instance, in many countries of occupied Europe.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know about any prison or detention unit that NLA had in 2001?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't come across any information suggesting that there could be a prison or a detention unit that the NLA had.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: From the materials that you reviewed before you prepared your report, had you seen any document that refers about their military police and whether they arrested anybody for violation of discipline or for committing a crime?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing any document suggesting that somebody was arrested. I --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Let me continue. Do you know about any court mechanism that had the power to deal with crimes and breaching of discipline? Any judicial mechanism.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the NLA? No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know about any documented evidence that anybody was appointed by NLA to be responsible for committed crimes by NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your question, sir. What do you exactly mean by saying "appointed"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: To be referred to a person as a perpetrator of a crime.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen any document that a person was designated to prosecute perpetrators of crime in NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean specifically a person within the NLA?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, person from NLA.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I didn't, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know about any procedures that have been initiated in structures of NLA against any of their members for committing a crime?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't come across any documents which would suggest these kind of procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Have you seen an order or other document that was signed by Gzim Ostreni before 2001. Before May 2001.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. But if you are specifically referring to the issue of discipline, I think I mentioned already in my previous testimony that I saw at least one document which was actually dated June 2001 and which was signed by --

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I apologise, I meant generally. I moved to another topic. I meant whether generally you have seen a document signed by Gzim Ostreni before May 2001. One more question. Have you seen an order by which Gzim Ostreni was appointed head of the -- or Chief of General Staff of the so-called NLA?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. I think it is time for a break, so I fulfilled my promise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Apostolski. We will adjourn now and resume at a quarter past.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, on Friday, the 19th of October, starting at about page 6556 of the transcript, my colleague Mr. Mettraux asked you about the term operational control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we please show the witness what is 65 ter 1D928, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: As page 6561 of the transcript, in response to Mr. Mettraux's question whether -- well, I'll wait for the document to come up. This is the Department of Defence of the United States Dictionary of Military and Associated Terms and at page 6561 of the transcript my colleague asked you whether you refer to this document in your amended expert report and you said: "If you specifically mean, sir, whether I quote this particular document in my report, whether it is mentioned in any of the footnotes, the answer, to the best of my knowledge, is no." Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is the top of page 2 of Exhibit P00466, Mr. Bezruchenko's amended expert report. And can we focus on the very top paragraph, please. And at the very top, there's a sentence that says: "Insurgency is commonly defined as 'an organised movement aimed at the overthrow of the constituted government through subversion an armed conflict.'" Do you see that sir?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then we see a footnote 2 and if we could focus now on what is footnote 2 towards the bottom of the page. Mr. Bezruchenko, footnote 2 refers us to the Dictionary of Military Terms, US Department of Defence, do you see that.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is it still correct that you did not cite to 65 ter 1D928, the document that was shown to you by my colleague?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not, sir. I apologise, I probably misspoke or misunderstood the question or perhaps I was misguided by the fact that I was shown the electronic version of the document, but of course said it in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness -- can we please turn to what is page 390 of this glossary. It has ERN number -- excuse me. I am going much too quickly. If we could turn back, please, to what is 65 ter number 1D928 and if we could turn to what is -- that is the correct page. Thank you very much. And at the bottom of that page we see the word "operation." If we could focus on the bottom of the English page, please. And you see, Mr. Bezruchenko, we see two definitions provided for the term "operation" in a military sense. The first one is "a military action or the carrying out of a strategic, operational, tactical, service, training or administrative military mission." Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the second definition says this: "The process of carrying on combat, including movement, supply, attack, defence, and manoeuvres needed to gain the objectives of any battle or campaign." Have you been following me, please?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we turn, please, to the next page of this document, it would be page 391 of this glossary. And we see here the definition of operational control. Actually if we could focus on the bottom of the page. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And this definition, this paragraph has been discussed with you at length. I'm not going to read the entire paragraph to you. But in the middle there's a sentence and it says: "Operational control includes authoritative direction over all aspects of military operations and joint training necessary to accomplish missions assigned to the command." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit 1D211, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I apologise, simply for the record, the document that Mr. Saxon has shown to the witness is admitted as Exhibit 1D252.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I apologise for giving the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is an investigator's note compiled by a witness in this case, Mr. Howard Tucker. Can we turn to the last page, please. It's from a meeting, 1300 hours in November, a Sunday in November, 2001, on the 10th of November. And you see there is a sentence in the middle of the page, Mr. Bezruchenko, beginning with the word: "However." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It says this: "However, Mr. Boskoski added some comments concerning the security issues involving Tetovo and stated that he would send armoured vehicles and suitably protected police into Tetovo to counter the violence (shooting incidents)." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would the deployment of officers like this and vehicles fall within the scope of operational control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At page 69 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honour. I have not objected so that the witness could give his evidence on that point. But this is not a document and not an issue which we have dealt with at all in relation to this particular document or the particular matters which we're to deal with with the witness. I mean, the witness is not a fact witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe there were several sessions of cross-examination devoted to the concept of operational control. I'm simply trying to clarify this concept and how it applies to the parties involved in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber sees to reason to interfere with the course of questioning, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, at page 6945 of the transcript my colleague Mr. Mettraux asked you whether the mobilisation of troops would be relevant to the concept of operational control. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you: Would a superior's power to demobilise troops also fall within the scope of operational control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir, definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness Exhibit 400 -- excuse me, Exhibit P402, please. And this would be from the section ERN N000-9607 to N000-9719 of the English translation, and would be page 36 within that range. This is the book published by Mr. Boskoski titled My Battle for Macedonia. And if we could focus perhaps on the second -- the lower half of this page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And the earlier paragraphs talk about the demonstrations after the withdrawal of the NLA from the area of Aracinovo. And then we see a paragraph near the bottom of the page, Mr. Bezruchenko, it begins with the phrase: "Two days later." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And Mr. Boskoski writes this: "Two days later on 29 June 2001, I announced demobilisation of the police reserve unit and their withdrawal from the areas around Skopje." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would the power to withdraw troops from an area also fall within the concept of operational control?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: At pages 6574 to 6576 on the 19th of October, 2007, my colleague asked you several questions about the role and the functions of the headquarters of the Ministry of the Interior that was known as Ramno. Do you remember that exchange?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Bezruchenko, on page 6575, you explained that while you did not review any orders specifically coming from the Ramno headquarters, you said you believe that this headquarters had a role in planning and carrying out operations. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit P00393. It is the annual report of the Ministry of Interior for 2001. First if you can simply show the title page, please, in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see, Mr. Bezruchenko, it says "Republic of Macedonia, Ministry of Interior," and below that it says "official secret, highly confidential." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And is that why you refer to this report I believe on Friday as a secret report, may have been Thursday.

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. It has been classified as official secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please turn to the ERN range N00-- for the English translation N005-0691 to N005-0699 to the first page of that range. And this will be page 73 of this report in the Macedonian version. And I'd like to focus, please, if we can on the third full paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see that paragraph, Mr. Bezruchenko, beginning with the phrase: "Because of further deterioration," do you see that, "of the situation"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And further down, we see on the 3rd of March, we see that the active and reserve police force was mobilised and raised to the highest level of combat mobility and readiness. And then we see in English a long sentence that says the following: "At the same time, because organised tactical and technical measures and actions had been undertaken for the discovery and preventing of terrorist and other types of criminal activities directed towards destabilizing the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia, an operation was initiated and an operational headquarters was established." Do you see that, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could we turn, please, to what is Exhibit - and I hope I give the right number this time - 1D12. No, this is not the right number. I'm looking for the decision of 7 March 2001, the decision to form the headquarters of Operative Action Ramno. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, this was the decision dated just four days after the large mobilisation of active and reserve police forces that we read about a moment ago. It was issued by Mr. Boskoski's predecessor as the minister of the interior and if we could focus, please on the word "decision" in paragraph 1. It would be a bit easier to read if we could highlight that. It says: "Decision to form the headquarters of the operative action Ramno." And then paragraph 1 says the following: "In order to organise, manage, coordinate and direct the measures and activities in connection with the operative action Ramno, headquarters are formed in the following composition," and then we see the members of that headquarters. Have you been following me, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we now please show the witness what is exhibit P00381. I see my colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply for the transcript we believe that the previous document or the document that is still on the screen is 1D112.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bezruchenko, exhibit P00381 is a decision dated the 29th of May, 2001, and it reads similarly to the decision that we just looked at. But, again, if we could focus our minds on the word "decision" through the first paragraph. It says this: "Decision to form the headquarters of operative action Ramno". And paragraph one it says: "In order to organise, manage, coordinate, and direct the measures and activities in connection with the operative action Ramno, headquarters are formed in the following composition," and we see that then Minister Boskoski has changed the composition of the members of the headquarters a bit. Mr. Bezruchenko, from a military perspective, what significance, if anything, do you see in the use of the verb "direct" in these decisions?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This clearly serves as indication that the headquarters of the operative action Ramno was actually giving powers to organise, deploy and control the forces of the Ministry of Interior in operational sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what -- can we show the witness Exhibit P34, please. And I'm just -- if we look at your last response in the transcript, Mr. Bezruchenko, it says, "the headquarters of operative action Ramno was actually giving powers to organise," et cetera. Did you say giving or given?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me say what I said precisely again, please. This clearly serves as an indication that the headquarters of the operative action Ramno was actually given powers to organise, deploy and control the forces of the Ministry of Interior in operational sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Bezruchenko, if you take a look at what is Exhibit P34, this is an order for performing service. It's dated the 12th of August, 2001, comes from the police station Mirkovci. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: It's an order given to several individuals and they're told in part 1 to control certain road segments.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry, Your Honours. Please bear with me for a moment. This is not the document that I wish to show at this time. I will move on. I will move on, Your Honours. Can we please show the witness what is Rule 65 ter, Prosecution's Rule 65 ter 260, please. Your Honours, this was a document that was seized during a suspect interview from Goran Mitevski who, in 2001, was the head or the director of the public security bureau of the Ministry of Interior. And it is dated 14th August 2001, it's from the Cair department of internal affairs, Skopje and it's entitled "Report on recorded events and measures undertaken regarding the Ramno/operative action." And if we can turn to the bottom of the second page, please, there's one more page. There's a description of some events of that day on the first page. And after a further description about an attempt to make an on-site investigation in the village of Ljuboten, the last paragraph, we see the following: "On 14 August 2001 at 1530 hours, pursuant to the Ramno operative action, four persons, citizens of the Republic of Macedonia, were detained by the Stankovec check-point. They are the following," and then some names are given. Do you see that, Mr. Bezruchenko?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: What significance, if anything, do you read from that phrase "pursuant to the Ramno operative action"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: My reading of this paragraph would be that, A, the operative action Ramno was going on as of 14 August 2001; and, B, that those individuals detained at the Stankovec check-point were in fact detained in the course of this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would this paragraph indicate that the person -- at least the person who wrote this -- wrote this document was aware of some kind of instructions pursuant to the operative action?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agree with your assumption, that would be indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour we object on a number of basis. The main being that the truth or reliability of anything contained in that document has not been established. The authenticity relies on Mr. Saxon's statement to the effect that the document came from Mr. Mitevski. We believe that to the extent that there was any comment that could be obtained or any evidence that could be drawn from the witness in relation to that document it's been properly put to the witness and Mr. Bezruchenko has given his opinion in relation to this particular document. We don't know what the author of that document meant by "pursuant to Ramno operative action." Mr. Bezruchenko has given an opinion. However, it is, I think, limited to that. Now the effort by the Prosecution to tender this document would require a person capable of giving evidence, as I mentioned, about the truth of the content, the reliability of the document, for instance, and in particular in relation it that sentence what was meant "pursuant to Ramno operative action."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there have been many, many documents admitted in this case through witnesses who did not write the document, had never seen the particular document before but were able to comment on some portion of the document. And so on its face, certainly, this document is similar to other documents that have been admitted by this Chamber, particularly in relation to the events of mid-August, around the village of Ljuboten. And therefore we see that there has at least been a sufficient level of authenticity and relevance for the admission of this document. How much weight the Chamber would choose to give this document at the end of the case, obviously that is another matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What is it that the Prosecution would seek to get from the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That there -- that police officers in mid-August 2001 were working according to some kind of -- to use the phrase of the document "operative action" or plan and were carrying out tasks pursuant to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you accept that the only witness who has spoken about that is the present witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, yes. I would have to do a transcript search to find others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The document will be received, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P490, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, what is Exhibit P00106.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Bezruchenko, this document comes from the internal affairs department of Cair. It's dated the 12th of August, 2001. And it's titled "Report on incidents recorded and measures undertaken under OA Ramno." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And below that there's description of a couple of events. From a military perspective, what significance, if anything, do you draw from this phrase "measures undertaken under OA Ramno"?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means for me a number of things. First of all it means that the signatory of this document was aware of the general plan and actions as stipulated by operation action Ramno which probably included a number of tasks and missions which were harmonized and coordinated both in space and in time. This would also mean that the actions as described in this report would fall into the category of tasks and missions pursuant to this operational action. In other words, that would mean that the actions undertaken were undertaken in agreement with the plan of operation Ramno.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness what is Prosecution 65 ter number 10 -- I see my colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I was waiting for you to finish your sentence. Yes, Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting the sentence. Your Honour, we would likely like to note it for the record both in relation to this document and the previous document that the Prosecution failed to put that material and that theory, to call it that, of an operation Ramno and the evidence that is now being led from any witness, factual witness who would have been capable of giving this evidence including from individuals who were related to this particular so-called operative action Ramno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, 65 ter 1032. Prosecution 65 ter 1032.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a document from police station Cair, Mr. Bezruchenko. And it describes time of -- it's an order to carry out a task on the 11th of August, 2001 from 0800 hours to 2000 hours on the same day. And it's an order to someone named Zoran Stojanovski and some other persons whose names are illegible and the concrete tasks are this: Between space and space "to be posted at the check-point and undertake full measures and activities in relation to operative action Ramno, checking identities, checking and searching individuals, vehicles and luggage." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VIKTOR BEZRUCHENKO [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
